Subject: Request: subprocessor delegation details + TLS cipher proof and SOC2/CAIQ evidence

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the productive call earlier. As part of our procurement and security review for the pilot, we need a compact evidence bundle focused on three items so we can clear legal and infosec gates this week:

1) Full list of subprocessors (names, primary function, hosting region) and an explicit statement which subprocessors process or can access plaintext customer payloads or keys.
2) Proof of TLS configuration and accepted cipher suites for your public endpoints (server certs, cipher list, and one-line explanation of forward secrecy posture).
3) Latest SOC 2 report (redacted OK) and a summarized CAIQ/SIG-lite matrix that maps critical controls to your evidence artifacts.

Target turnaround: 5 business days from today (we're aiming to start onboarding first workloads 2026-06-10). If any items require extra approvals or NDAs, flag them now. Also let me know if any subprocessors are hosted in APAC (we have regional data residency needs).

Please send anything as attachments or links to a shared Drive. If you prefer, a short cover note describing where keys are stored, key ownership, and whether KMS is customer- or provider-managed will help speed review.

Appreciate it — Amira

--
Amira Hassan
Security & Compliance Lead, Acme Biomed

Subject: Draft: subprocessor inventory + access characterization

Evelyn / Jordan / Amira —

Attached is the initial subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_20260530.csv) and a short plain-English summary below. Full inventory in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-acme-evidence (drive stubs attached).

Summary (high level):
- Hosting / compute: NimbusCloud (us-west2) — handles GPU inference runtime, does not have access to KMS keys; only processes encrypted payloads when customer opts into provider-managed keys.
- Caching & batching: CacheFlow (us-east1) — plaintext caching limited to ephemeral prefixes; only stores truncated tokens; no long-term customer payload retention.
- Secrets / KMS: KeyHarbor (us-central1) — KMS provider used for provider-managed key workflows. By default keys are customer-managed in BYOK mode; we only have access where customers opt in to provider key hosting.
- Observability: Tracelytics (saas) — collects telemetry & error traces; payload scrubbing applied via filters before export; access limited to redwood-infra SRE accounts.

Access to plaintext / keys:
- For customers using provider-managed keys, KeyHarbor holds wrapped keys necessary to decrypt during runtime; Redwood's runtime uses a short-lived wrapped key material and does not persist plaintext keys. For BYOK, KeyHarbor never receives plaintext keys.
- Only a small set of cleared platform engineers (on-call SRE rotations) have emergency access flows to decrypt payloads; these flows are logged and audited.

Attachments included: (stub) subprocessors_20260530.csv

If you want, I can add a per-subprocessor column for evidenced controls (SOC/ISO cert present, Data Processing Agreement signed, Data Flow diagram).

Ben
Senior Security Programs, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. Two follow-ups: 

1) Can you explicitly flag any subprocessors that process customer-controlled PII (we have a subset of PHI-like identifiers in our test payloads)?
2) Procurement has asked that any APAC hosting be called out (we need regional-specific approvals). You mentioned no planned APAC subprocessors for customer-managed workflows, but please confirm any APAC presence for telemetry/analytics or third-party backup services.

Separately, can we get a short CAIQ/SIG-lite mapping that maps your listed subprocessors to the specific CAIQ questions (network encryption, key management, logging, data retention)? A 1-page summary per subprocessor would be ideal.

Procurement also wants to see a DocuSignable statement of subprocessor delegation + exemplar DPA clause. When you have a package, please upload the SOC2 redacted copy, the cipher suite proof, and the CAIQ summary to the Drive link and send a DocuSign link to procurement@acme-bio.com.

If it helps, I'll accept a phased delivery (inventory + TLS first, then CAIQ + SOC2).

—Amira

Amira / procurement —

Attached is the evidence bundle we discussed. Items uploaded to Drive and included as redacted attachments below:
- redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20260530.pdf (per-subprocessor table with region, function, and data-access characterization)
- tls_cipher_report_20260530.pdf (server cert fingerprint, accepted cipher suites, forward secrecy notes)
- SOC2_Signed_Redwood_2025.pdf (redacted)
- CAIQ_summary_20260530.xlsx (SIG-lite mapping & per-subprocessor 1-pagers)
- subprocessors_20260530.csv (raw export)

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC-123-ACME-Redwood (covers subprocessor delegation statement + exemplar DPA clause).

Key clarifications:
- APAC presence: Tracelytics (analytics) has an APAC egress endpoint that stores only aggregated telemetry; no customer payload or keys are stored in APAC. This is called out in the inventory file.
- KMS: Default workflow is BYOK (customer-managed). If customer opts into provider-hosted keys, KeyHarbor operates in a provable HSM-backed mode; Jordan included the KMS attestation in the TLS/KMS pdf.
- Emergency decrypt: emergency access is audited, requires 2-person SRE approval, and is logged to immutable audit.

Next steps: procurement/infosec review, then DPA signature via DocuSign. If you need any live evidence (e.g., a short walkthrough of the KMS key lifecycle), Ben & Jordan can arrange a 30-min session next week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
